paragraphs: Decision center: the work of a desktop publisher is to lay out text, charts and images according to established design and page specifications into a finished product that can go directly to print or online — studying page or design instructions, importing text and art elements, selecting type size and font style and column width and spacing, producing sample page layouts, checking and correcting proofs, determining color separations and converting file formats. The focus of judgment is not whether you can use a particular piece of software, but whether you can verify every step along the chain of taking the job and reading the instructions — layout — proofing and correction — output and delivery, and clearly state which decisions must be handed back to design or editorial.

Worth trying first: you are willing to sit in front of a screen for long periods doing detailed proofreading, willing to repeatedly adjust according to established font, column width and spacing specifications without rushing, able to accept repeated proofs and revisions, willing to confirm design intent and the scope of authorization before making changes, and able to write file naming, versions and delivery requirements clearly.

Requires caution: if you are impatient about checking word by word and page by page, tend to discover layout errors only at the last moment, or are unwilling to accept multiple rounds of client and editorial revisions, or habitually change confirmed design specifications based on personal aesthetics without communicating first, then the actual work experience usually does not match expectations.

Low-risk verification: use the complete D07 specifications, manuscripts and proofs from the getting-started section, compare on paper the three field differences of heading 12→14pt, body 8→10pt and file v1→v2, and write four works plus equipment/bleed items to be verified. You may use your own tools for layout; this does not prove real software proficiency, print delivery or job qualification.

Decision center: whether design specifications, manuscripts and image elements can be turned into a set of page files and delivery records that colleagues can understand, the next person taking over can reproduce, and the print shop or the online launch step will not get wrong.

The work is mainly indoors in front of a computer: email accounts for 100% every day, a controlled indoor environment 94% every day, face-to-face discussion with individuals and teams 76% every day, sitting continuously or almost continuously 74%, time pressure 64% every day; using hands to handle or feel objects and tools 63% (continuously or almost continuously), repetitive motions more than half the time 40%, continuous contact with others 48%; precision or accuracy being very important 30%, limited decision freedom 48%. The pace is often determined by delivery deadlines and multiple rounds of revision, and detailed proofreading and version management are daily routines.

This page is fixed to 43-9031 Desktop Publishers; the tasks include page design and proofreading text corrections, overlapping with design, editorial and proofreading. Art directors focus on overall direction and the team, print and postpress focus on physical craft, and web development focuses on code and applications; compare by actual output and authorization, and do not exclude tasks by name.

Inputs that must be verified: design specifications and page requirements (fonts, type sizes, column widths, spacing, color and separation requirements), the source and usage authorization of manuscripts and images, the output purpose (print, electronic or web) and the corresponding file format, proof versions and revision records, and delivery time and naming conventions. What must not be done: do not change confirmed design specifications or uncleared materials without authorization, do not deliver without checking proofs, do not omit confirmation of file format and color mode, and do not leave file versions that cannot be traced.

Fit judgments should be made in combination with actual layout task performance, proof accuracy and collaboration feedback, and should not be replaced by self-assessment of aesthetics or a self-perceived sense of software proficiency; patience for detail, tolerance for multiple rounds of revision and the degree of attention to delivery specifications all need to be confirmed in real tasks and reviews.

D07 is entirely fictional, for electronic preview and field verification only. Real projects require checking material licenses, output specifications and the release process; China's Order No. 37 states that publishing professional work also involves qualification registration and responsible editor registration, and prepress skill standards must be checked separately; qualification cannot be obtained through the exercises on this page.

The object of this occupation's work is the page to be published: text content, graphic and image elements, font and layout parameters, color and separation settings, and the final output file format; the outputs are page files that can go directly to print or online, proofs and delivery records; the basis for judgment is design specifications and page requirements, material usage authorization, output purpose and prepress standards, rather than personal aesthetic preferences.

Desktop publishers also design page layouts, produce samples and check and correct proofs; BLS explicitly lists possibly correcting spelling, punctuation and grammar and collaborating with authors on images. Graphic designers focus on commercial visual concepts, art directors coordinate visual direction and the team, editors focus on content organization, and proofreaders focus on errors; the work overlaps, and specific content changes, approval and release follow position authorization — occupational titles cannot be used to exclude design or text correction. Related original verification background: Judgment one: whether the page is faithful to the design specifications — whether fonts, type sizes, column widths, spacing and alignment are executed according to specification, and whether a confirmed design is changed without communication.

The work of a desktop publisher can be divided into three linked but independent work areas. The first is page design and layout: studying page or design instructions to determine the work to be done and the order of operations, using software to import text and art elements (electronic clip art, scans or digital photos), keying in text and selecting type size, font style, column width and spacing, and producing sample page layouts for approval. The second is graphic and image processing and proofing: using pixel or bitmap editing, airbrushing, masking and retouching to process graphics and photos, entering image coordinates and color specifications for retouching and color correction, selecting the number of colors and determining separations, and checking preliminary and final proofs and correcting errors. The third is output and collaborative delivery: converting various files into formats for print or the internet, delivering publication masters to printers to produce film and printing plates, collaborating with graphic artists, editors and writers to produce master copies according to design specifications, and filing copies of publications and version records. The three work areas proceed according to the delivery flow, and the pace is determined by deadlines and revision rounds. Related original verification background: Judgment two: whether manuscripts and images are usable and compliant — whether the text is complete, whether there is garbled text or missing characters, whether image resolution and color mode meet the output purpose, and whether materials have a verifiable source and usage authorization.

Judgment three: whether proof errors are found and corrected — whether preliminary and final proofs are checked page by page, and whether typos, misplacement, mismatched graphics and text, and page order problems are corrected and documented before delivery.

Related original verification background: Judgment four: whether output settings are correct — whether the number of colors and separations, bleed and margins, and file format and version are consistent with print or launch requirements, and whether a verifiable check was done before delivery.

Judgment five: whether collaboration and authorization boundaries are clear — which changes need to go back to design, editorial or the client for confirmation, which are layout adjustments this position may handle on its own, and whether communication follows the process rather than changing first and reporting afterwards.

Judgment six: whether versions and delivery are traceable — whether file naming, version numbers, revision notes and delivery channels are complete, and whether the print shop or the launch step can reproduce the final page from the delivery records.

Core purpose

Lay out text and images according to established design specifications into a finished product that can go directly to print or online, and ensure the page is accurate, the materials are compliant and the delivery is usable.

Core purposes of adjacent positions: graphic designers establish visual concepts and layout schemes; art directors guard overall visual direction and consistency; editors and proofreaders ensure content accuracy and error-free text; print and postpress positions turn the page into a physical object; web and front-end positions turn the design into a launchable page.
Main objects and basis

The objects are text, graphic and image elements, font and layout parameters, color and separation settings and output file formats; the basis is design specifications and page requirements, material usage authorization, output purpose and prepress standards.

Objects and basis of adjacent positions: visual concepts and layout schemes (design specifications and brand guidelines); overall visual direction (brand and project requirements); text content and error standards (editorial and proofreading specifications); printing and binding craft (print and postpress process requirements); web implementation (front-end technology and accessibility requirements).
Core process
Read specifications and take the job → layout and graphic and image processing → produce proofs → check and correct → determine separations and format → deliver and file.

Main outputs

Responsible parties

People in this occupation are responsible for the accuracy of the pages, graphic and image processing and proofs they complete, and for the completeness and traceability of delivery files; when design specifications are unclear or material authorization is unclear, they should confirm first and then act, and must not make content decisions on behalf of clients or editors.

Responsible parties of adjacent positions: graphic designers are responsible for the visual scheme; art directors are responsible for overall visual direction; editors and proofreaders are responsible for content and text errors; print and postpress positions are responsible for physical quality; web and front-end positions are responsible for page implementation and launch.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with graphic artists, editors, writers, clients and the print shop according to the process, confirm design intent and the scope of authorization before changes, and explain file format and version at delivery; raise and report content changes that exceed one's duties or authorization first.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: graphic designers collaborate with clients and art directors; art directors collaborate with the project team; editors and proofreaders collaborate with authors and layout; print and postpress positions collaborate with prepress and logistics; web and front-end positions collaborate with design and back end.

How to start and what to prepare

The following stages and directions are a capability development structure summarized by the editor, not a uniform industry rank table, hiring condition or years table guaranteeing promotion; qualification, skill level and delivery authorization requirements are verified according to the target jurisdiction, unit type and project conditions.

BLS typical entry-level associate degree, about 1 month of on-the-job training; those with experience and software proficiency may not hold a college degree, and some employers prefer a bachelor's degree. The None for related experience in Table 1.2 is a typical classification and does not exempt skills testing; the 1—2 years of O*NET Job Zone Three is an occupational group preparation description, not a uniform term for this occupation. Order No. 37 applies to the listed content processing and binding and layout of publishing units, and to proofreading of newspapers and news periodicals, while news gathering and editing are governed separately. Applicable personnel must obtain qualification and register within 2 years of starting the job, and responsible editors must have intermediate or above qualifications before starting and be registered. Presidents, editors-in-chief, chief editors, editorial office directors and their deputies must have intermediate or above qualifications and complete registration procedures; it does not place all commercial typesetting or all production supervisors within this scope. The 2019 standard for prepress processing and production operators 6-08-01-01 covers graphic and image processing, layout and imposition and plate making, from level five to level one; the general education requirement of high school or equivalent and the color vision requirement belong to that standard and are not extended to all United States desktop publishing positions. Level five may count 1 year of accumulated service in this or a related occupation or completion of an apprenticeship; level four may follow level five plus 4 years, 6 accumulated years, or the listed graduation paths in related majors; the remaining levels are verified separately for their specific conditions. Theory and skills each require a passing score of 60 on the percentage scale, and technicians and senior technicians undergo an additional comprehensive review. description.text: Desktop Publishers (O*NET-SOC 43-9031.00) use computer software to lay out manuscripts and graphic elements and produce material that can be used directly for publication: reading design specifications and layout instructions, importing text and art elements, selecting type size and font style and column width and spacing, producing sample page layouts, processing graphics and photos with retouching and color correction, selecting the number of colors and determining separations, checking proofs page by page and correcting them, and converting files into formats for print or the internet and delivering masters to printers. The work is mainly indoors in front of a computer, with frequent email and communication (100% every day), continuous sitting 74%, time pressure 64% every day, and precision or accuracy being very important 30%. United States scope: in the 2025 wage data the median annual wage is 55,290 USD (median hourly 26.58 USD), with annual percentiles of 35,680 / 43,730 / 55,290 / 73,840 / 96,170 USD; 2024 employment is about 5,000 people, a decline is projected for 2024—2034 with about 400 projected openings; the interest code is CAR. Mainland China: for professional publishing technical work you may take the professional qualification examination for publishing professionals, and the prepress and plate-making direction corresponds to the prepress processing and production operator occupational skill level (level five to level one, requiring normal color vision with no color blindness or color weakness); public statistics have not established an occupational-level wage scope for this occupation, and this page marks the gap in the relevant places.

subject.summary: Desktop publishers (43-9031.00) use software to design and lay out graphics and text, check and correct proofs and convert delivery files. In the United States the May 2025 median annual wage is 55,290 USD; the older 2024—34 annual average openings are 400, while the new 2025—35 employment declines by 14% with 300 annual average openings, and the overall projection is not AI attribution. In China, qualification registration applies to the listed publishing professional work, and responsible editors must also have intermediate or above qualifications and be registered; prepress skill recognition is verified separately. Chinese industry annual average references are shown in the salary section split into private and non-private. Precise occupational wages and occupational AI adoption effects were not obtained.
